source0_callback_breakpoint.limitation: No source-0 dispatch was observed in this run; this does not prove one can never occur in another execution state.

retail_callback_semantics.source1_branch: Optionally calls the callback at the structure referenced by object+10900 (function pointer at +16, data at +20), then performs the associated spinlock/bit cleanup. It has no direct call to 0x823A4640.
retail_callback_semantics.source0_branch: Checks GPU MMIO register 0x7FC86544 bit 0 and calls 0x823A4640 when the bit is set.
retail_callback_semantics.xex_identity: The generated source belongs to the locked retail XEX identity above.

current_process2_source_review.observed_behavior: SetInterruptCallback stores the callback. The sole ExecuteInterrupt call dispatches PM4_INTERRUPT with args {1u, callback_data}; no source-0/vblank dispatch was found in this plugin source.

rexglue_default_vblank_reference.behavior: GraphicsSystem::MarkVblank calls DispatchInterruptCallback(0, 2). The custom shift-native plugin path reviewed above does not call this method.

interpretation.supported: This Linux run delivered PM4 source-1 callbacks to the exact retail callback, while the completion predicate byte and object+13432 remained unchanged during the observed interval. Source 0 was not observed. The latest Process 2 plugin source reviewed here contains PM4 source-1 routing but no source-0/vblank dispatch.
interpretation.candidate_blocker: Missing source-0/vblank delivery is a concrete Process 2 integration gap to investigate. Process 1 did not alter guest state or renderer code.
interpretation.not_proven: This does not prove source-0/vblank absence is the cause of the software-queue wait, nor that implementing it alone will reach the frontend or a race. The tested plugin binary is identified by hash, but its build commit is not independently bound to the latest Process 2 source commit. No visible retail frame or playable state is claimed.
